Published online:
July 7, 2026

Geographic focus:
United States (Wall Street / Major US Financial Institutions)

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical observation [YES] — Q2 2026 results, H1 2026 IB revenue data
T2. Forward-looking immediate [YES] — Q2 earnings reports due July 14–15; H2 2026 outlook
T3. Long-term development [NO]

Synopsis:
US Wall Street banks are set to report strong Q2 2026 earnings driven by a surge in sales & trading (equities leading, boosted by the ~$86B SpaceX IPO), robust investment banking fees (global IB revenue +24% YoY to $61.4B in H1 2026), accelerating loan growth, and expanding net interest margins. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are expected to outperform on equities. Key risks to monitor: potential sequential slowdown in trading vs. Q1, inflation pressure on consumers, credit quality, and geopolitical uncertainty. All six major banks report July 14–15.
